title: Segmentation-driven hierarchical cache and batch orchestrator with safe apply/rollback
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a hierarchical per-customer and per-route cache+batch orchestration layer that generates actionable recommendations (batch sizes, KV/prefix caching rules, TTLs) and applies them using a guarded rollout (dry-run -> canary -> staged roll).

Problem statement: Customers and routes have widely varying request shapes (short chat vs long generation, embeddings vs chat contexts). One-size-fits-all batching/caching policies either leave cost on the table or increase tail latency and quality regression risk. We need automated, segmented policies that 1) reduce per-token unit cost, 2) respect latency SLOs, and 3) can be safely applied and rolled back with auditability.

Design summary:
- Segmentation model: routes and customers are classified into tiers (Gold/Silver/Bronze) plus a special 'sensitive' segment for high-regulatory customers. Classification uses historical telemetry: median tokens/request, 95th latency, cacheable-prefix ratio, and business tier.
- Policy primitives: allowed batch window (ms), max batch size, KV cache TTL, prefix-only caching toggle, per-route allowlist/denylist for aggressive prefetching, and quantization profile suggestions.
- Hierarchical override: global -> tier -> customer -> route. More specific entries win. Operators can pin or lock customer-level configs.
- Recommendation engine: runs nightly simulation on 7-day traffic windows to produce delta estimates (cost %, expected change in p95 latency, cache-hit%). Recommendations include conservative and aggressive options with expected unit-cost savings.
- Dry-run and scoring: before applying, a dry-run mode routes a small percentage of traffic to a simulated executor that records real effects (effective batch sizes, added latency percentiles, cache eviction rate). Scoring function yields PASS / REVIEW / FAIL.
- Guarded rollout: staged canary (1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic abort on: >5% regression in p95 latency, >2% customer error-rate increase, or cost change outside predicted bounds. All steps logged to audit trail with operator-notes required on manual overrides.
- Allowlist/Denylist semantics: allowlist entries enable aggressive batching/prefetch for specific routes/customers where we have regression tests; denylist entries disable automatic changes for sensitive traffic. Denylists are enforced at evaluation time and in dry-run.
- Safe rollback: automated rollback path triggers if canary/metrics thresholds breached; rollback includes warm-revert to previous cache state where possible (explicit cache invalidation avoided during rollback unless operator approves).
- Observability: per-change dashboard with token-level cost delta, batch size histogram, cache hit curve, and per-customer trace examples. Integrations with Console rollouts and existing tracing.

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive batching reduces cost but can increase tail latency for short-lived interactive routes; hence tiering and route allowlist needed.
- Prefetching increases cache memory pressure; TTL heuristics and eviction awareness included.
- Dry-run complexity vs. speed: chosen to be nightly simulation + small live dry-run to balance fidelity and cost.

Deliverables:
1) Orchestrator service prototype (API + controller) that ingests recommendations and exposes apply/dry-run/cancel endpoints.
2) Nightly simulator job and recommendation report generator.
3) Canary rollout actuator with RBAC and operators UI hooks in Console.
4) Runbook for manual intervention and incident postmortem templates.

Success metrics: average per-token cost reduction for eligible routes (target 12% median), no more than 1% of customers seeing >10% p95 latency regression during rollouts, and audit log coverage for 100% of policy changes.
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation engine produces per-customer/per-route recommendations and stores them in the policy store
Dry-run mode captures simulator metrics and yields PASS/REVIEW/FAIL scores
Guarded rollout orchestrator can run staged canaries with automated aborts based on telemetry
Allowlist/denylist rules respected at evaluation and apply time
Automated rollback triggers and rollback completes within defined SLOs (target: <5 minutes to revert config)
Console shows per-change cost/latency dashboard and links to audit record
